A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same generator-based adversarial attack research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison despite the changed title and substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v4 reports original transfer-attack experiments, component and block ablations, defense evaluations, and supplementary GPT and LLaVA results.

after.justification: v5 retains original attack experiments and reports additional foreground-IoU, spectral-energy, and alternative-surrogate cross-task results.

M1.justification: The EMA teacher, early-block cosine-hinge consistency loss, baseline adversarial objectives, and teacher-based inference remain. The U-Net bottleneck adaptation already appears in v4. Renaming the framework SCGA and replacing distillation terminology with consistency terminology do not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: v5 adds ImageNet-S foreground-mask evaluation to probe generator-feature alignment in Figure 1 and Appendix D. The existing classification domains, Cityscapes segmentation, COCO detection and captioning, and ImageNet-R zero-shot evaluation remain represented; the multimodal tasks were already present in v4.

E2.justification: The six principal attack baselines remain CDA, LTP, BIA, GAMA, FACL, and PDCL. However, v4 Table 5 compares BIA against BIA with the proposed method across perturbation budgets, whereas v5 Table S3 reports only the augmented method, removing the comparator from that sweep. Newly discussed diffusion and intermediate-level attacks are not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Reported settings change through HRNet's removal from the cross-model panel, surrogate-dependent victim substitutions involving VGG-16/19 in Table S8, and removal of the LLaVA-13B configuration. The budget sweep changes its grid and reported metrics. New diagnostics introduce foreground clustering and spectral-band measurements; Figure S10 changes its stated threshold from 0.2 to 0.6 with min-max normalization. These changes do not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v5 adds quantitative tests of semantic drift across generator blocks and changes in low/high-frequency feature energy (Figure 1, Table 6, Appendix D), substantially extending v4's visual mechanism evidence. It also extends alternative-surrogate analysis to segmentation and detection and adds metrics to classification ablations. Conversely, U-Net classification ablations and parts of the earlier budget-robustness comparison disappear.

E5.justification: The three random trials and their mean-plus-standard-deviation results are identical in v4 Table S11 and v5 Table S13. No additional runs, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures are reported. The new cross-block IoU standard deviation is a semantic-variability metric, not experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Cross-model results are extensively revised: CDA's average accuracy delta changes from -11.27 to -6.89 percentage points, while the DenseNet-169-surrogate BIA delta changes from +1.48 to -2.90. These are replaced results under revised victim panels, not established same-setting gains. v5 also adds foreground-IoU, spectral-energy, and alternative-surrogate cross-task results, while removing absolute baseline entries from the alternative-surrogate cross-model table and the LLaVA-13B captioning results.

T1.justification: v4 Equation 1 incorrectly uses student parameters in both weighted terms of the EMA update. v5 Equation 2 correctly incorporates the previous teacher parameters. This repairs the mathematical recurrence while retaining the EMA procedure described in both versions. The hinge loss and classification-metric definitions remain equivalent; no theorem or proof development is added.

C1.justification: The abstract and first contribution in v5 explicitly claim that lower cross-block foreground-IoU variability is associated with stronger transfer, extending v4's claim about early-block semantic retention. The central contributions of generator-level consistency guidance, compatibility with existing attacks, and ACR-based evaluation remain.

C2.justification: v5 adds substantial spectral and foreground-coherence explanations, attributes limited dense-prediction gains to the hinge margin's emphasis on coarse structure, and expands discussion of CLIP compatibility and alternative foundation models. Appendix D also introduces practical defender interpretations of ACR. Its new claim that approximately 14% ACR minus 8% ASR yields a 6% net accuracy benefit incorrectly subtracts rates conditioned on different subsets.

D1.justification: v5 supplies processing details for foreground clustering and spectral analysis, including the frequency cutoff of 0.2, and specifies VGG pooling-layer resolutions and feature-map normalization. The existing optimizer, epoch count, learning rate, principal hyperparameters, GPU, and computational measurements remain. Both versions promise code release upon publication.

R1.justification: Appendices B-D substantially expand research positioning through diffusion-based attacks, detailed distinctions from ILA/ILA++/ILPD/TAP, semantic-information literature, and proposed compatibility with spatially sensitive foundation models such as DINOv2 and SAM. These extend the earlier generator-versus-surrogate distinction beyond merely relocating related work or changing citation style.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and contribution narrative are substantially rewritten around SCGA and semantic consistency. Background and motivation replace related work in the main-text sequence, while related work and implementation settings move to reorganized appendices. This is extensive narrative restructuring beyond terminology replacement.

P2.justification: v5 redraws the pipeline with explicit training and evaluation stages, expands the motivation figure into a composite diagnostic, and moves the original overview plot to the conclusion. It merges domain/task and ablation tables, replaces named victim headers with letter codes, changes highlighting, and redraws feature-difference visualizations. These are substantial display changes beyond numerical updates and renumbering.

improvement.justification: v5 adds useful quantitative mechanism evidence in Figure 1 and Table 6 and corrects the EMA equation. However, its new Appendix D argument claims an accuracy benefit from subtracting differently conditioned ACR and ASR values, although the reported cross-domain accuracy falls from 90.85% clean to 84.95% at epsilon 4. Revised Table S8 also conflicts with the retained interpretation of DenseNet-169 results. The explanatory gains coexist with new correctness and reporting problems, preventing a reliable net-quality judgment.
